        Dearborn County Lateral Project

        Minor Workspace/Alignment Updates and Environmental Correspondence

Dear Ms. Reese:


On May 29, 2026, Texas Gas Transmission, LLC (“Texas Gas”) submitted an Abbreviated Application for
a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity Authorization for the Dearborn County Lateral Project
(“Project”) in the subject docket. Since the filing of the application, Texas Gas has incorporated minor
modifications to the proposed Project to reduce environmental impacts, address constructability issues, and
accommodate landowner requests.

Minor Workspace/Alignment Updates

Texas Gas prepared this supplemental filing to provide the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
(“Commission”) with updated information relating to minor reroutes of the Project’s mainline and minor
workspace modifications that have occurred subsequent to the May 29, 2026 certificate application filing.
The re-routes and modifications reflected in these supplemental filing materials have resulted in a decrease
in overall permanent impacts from the proposed Project, including a reduction in length of the pipeline
route and a reduction in overall Project workspace. This reduction in acreage, as well as modifications to
the pipeline route to avoid and/or minimize impacts on sensitive environmental and cultural areas, has also
decreased impacts to both wetlands and waterbodies.

Landowner Updates

The minor alignment and workspace updates will not impact any new landowners. In addition, Texas Gas
notes that they continue to be actively engaged with their landowners and have acquired tracts for
approximately 32% of the landowners.

Environmental

The updated information includes environmental survey results, agency correspondence, and other
supporting environmental documentation developed since the filing of the application, reflecting continued
consultation and coordination with federal and state agencies. Texas Gas is also providing updated
 alignment sheets, construction drawings, and environmental report appendices to support project
modifications implemented to reduce environmental impacts, address constructability considerations, and
accommodate landowner requests. These updates include completed geotechnical investigations, additional
wetland and waterbody delineations, and revisions to previously filed resource report tables and exhibits.

The enclosed Supplemental Filing includes the following components:

 ATTACHMENT 1:            PUBLIC                        Project Modification Maps

 ATTACHMENT 2:            PUBLIC                        Supplemental Filing Summary, Including
                                                        Narrative Updates to Resource Reports 1, 2, 3, 4,
                                                        6, 7, and 8, and Revised Tables, Appendices,
                                                        Figures, and Other Supporting Documentation

 ATTACHMENT 2:            PRIVILEGED                    Alignment Sheets with sensitive data


Pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 388.112 of the Commission’s Regulations, Texas Gas respectfully requests that the
information in Attachment 2 – PRIVILEGED be accorded privileged and confidential treatment. The
information contained herein clearly marked and labeled “CUI//PRIV” and “CONTAINS PRIVILEGED
INFORMATION – DO NOT RELEASE” is being submitted to the Commission on October 21, 2026,
and should maintain such designation for the life of the assets to which such information pertains as its
release, when combined with publicly available information, may possibly place the assets and personnel
of Texas Gas at undue risk.

The undersigned is the authorized representative and should be considered the respondent to this filing. If you
have any questions or need additional information, please contact me at (713) 321-8420 or at
shannon.miller@bwpipelines.com.

 Supplemental Filing Summary
         On May 29, 2026, Texas Gas Transmission, LLC (Texas Gas) filed an application with the
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC or the Commission) pursuant to Section 7(c) of
the Natural Gas Act and Part 157 of the Commission’s regulations, seeking authorization for
construction and operation of the Dearborn County Lateral Project (Project; Docket No. CP26-
536-000). Since the filing of the application, Texas Gas has incorporated minor modifications to
the proposed Project to reduce environmental impacts, address constructability issues, and
accommodate landowner requests.

         The purpose of this filing is to provide an overview of the proposed workspace and
alignment modifications and to provide FERC with updated information regarding the associated
impacts on the relevant resources discussed in Resource Reports 1 through 12 submitted as part
of the application. This filing also provides the results of the Phase 2a geotechnical investigations,
which was recently filed with FERC on October 16, 2026, as well as additional wetland and
waterbody surveys completed to date, habitat reconnaissance surveys for mussels that have
been completed to date, an updated landowner list with mailing address revisions and change in
ownership, and documentation of agency correspondence not previously filed.

         In total, Texas Gas has incorporated 12 modifications to the proposed Project. These
modifications have resulted in a net increase in construction-related temporary impacts by 7.84
acres (3.94 percent) and a net decrease in operation-related permanent impacts by 2.50 acres

 RESOURCE REPORT 1
Section 1.1            Project Description

       Texas Gas has filed an Abbreviated Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience
and Necessity with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for authorization to construct and
operate the Project. The Project is designed to provide 265,000 dekatherms per day of firm
natural gas transportation service to Vistra Corp.’s Miami Fort Power Plant in support of its
planned conversion from coal to natural gas. Specifically, Texas Gas is proposing to:

          construct and operate 11.59 miles of 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline from
           Dearborn County, Indiana to Hamilton County, Ohio;

          construct and operate tie-in piping, a pig launcher, and associated infrastructure to the
           existing Texas Gas 26-inch-diameter Mainline System in Dearborn County, Indiana
           (hereafter referred to as the “Tie-In Facility”);

          construct and operate a new measurement and flow control station and associated
           infrastructure in Dearborn County, Indiana (hereafter referred to as the “M&R Station”);
           and

          construct and operate a new pig receiver and associated infrastructure in Hamilton
           County, Ohio (hereafter referred to as the “Interconnect Facility”).

Section 1.1.2          Location and Description of Facilities

Pipeline Facilities

       Approximately 59 percent (6.95 miles) of the new Dearborn County Lateral will be co-
located with existing utility rights-of-way (ROWs).


RESOURCE REPORT 2
Section 2.3            Surface Water Resources

       Due to accessibility constraints and ongoing constructability and engineering analysis,
field surveys have not been completed and are currently ongoing. However, biological field
surveys have been completed along approximately 90 percent of the overall environmental survey
area (ESA).




                                                   7
 Section 2.3.1          Waterbodies Crossed or Otherwise Impacted by the Project Facilities

         Texas Gas has identified 136 waterbody crossings within the Project area. Of these, 90
were identified as ephemeral streams, 24 as intermittent streams, 18 as perennial streams, 2 as
manmade ponds, and 2 as natural ponds. Of the total waterbody crossings, 14 are classified as
major waterbodies, of which 4 will be crossed by horizontal directional drill, 2 will be crossed via
the open-cut method, and the remaining will be crossed via timber mats or new temporary
culverts. Eighteen of the total waterbody crossings are classified as intermediate waterbodies
and 104 are classified as minor waterbodies, the majority of which will be crossed via the open-
cut method.

Section 2.3.3          Public Watershed Areas

         The Project is located within Zone II of the Louisville Water Company SWPA in Kentucky
from MP 5.93 to MP 11.23 EQ; however, the nearest surface water intake for the Louisville Water
Company is the Crescent Hill Water Treatment Plant, approximately 71 miles south of the Project
workspace (Kentucky Energy and Environment Cabinet [KEEC], 2026).

Section 2.3.4          Floodplains

         According to the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), 2.33 miles of the
Dearborn County Lateral and 5.56 acres of access roads occur within the 100-year floodplain
(Zone A and Zone AE) (FEMA, 2026). A total of 0.37 mile of the proposed Dearborn County
Lateral is located in Zone X (shaded), which is subject to the 0.2 percent chance of an annual
flood event and is located between the limits of the 100-year floodplain and 500-year floodplain
(FEMA, 2026, 2020a).

Section 2.4.1          Existing Wetland Resources

         Wetland delineations were conducted for the Project in October 2025, from January 2026
through April 2026, and in September 2026 in accordance with the Regional Supplement to the
Corps of Engineers Wetland Delineation Manual: Eastern Mountains and Piedmont Region
(Version 2.0) (USACE, 2012b) and the routine determination guidelines provided in the U.S. Army
Corps of Engineers (USACE) Wetland Delineation Manual (Technical Report Y-87-1) (USACE,
1987).




                                                 8
 RESOURCE REPORT 3
Section 3.1            Introduction

       Habitat assessments were conducted in October 2025, from January 2026 through April
2026, and in September 2026.

Section 3.2.1          Fishery Classification

       Texas Gas has identified 136 waterbodies crossing within the Project area. Of these, 90
were identified as ephemeral streams, 24 as intermittent streams, 18 as perennial streams, 2 as
manmade ponds, and 2 as natural ponds.

Section 3.2.2          Fisheries of Special Concern

       Waterbodies with fisheries of special concern include those that support fisheries of
exceptional recreational value, such as trout populations; those that provide habitat for a protected
species; or those that are assigned a special state fishery management designation. State and
federal agencies may regulate these waterbodies by imposing timing restrictions for in stream
activities and/or specialized construction techniques.        However, through discussions with
Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (KDFWR) regarding the Project, Texas Gas
received approval to conduct in-stream activities outside of June 1 through November 30 in
waterbodies in Kentucky (Appendix 1C). Based on correspondence with Indiana Department of
Natural Resources (IDNR), there are no required time of year restrictions for in-stream
construction for stream crossings that would not also require an IDNR floodway permit or that
meet the applicable utility exemption (Buffington, 2026). Water withdrawal activities at Tanner’s
Creek will require an IDNR floodway permit; therefore, Texas Gas will coordinate with IDNR
regarding the applicability of a time of year restrictions for water withdrawal activities in Indiana.
Texas Gas is continuing to consult with Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR) regarding
in-stream construction restriction windows and will submit any additional correspondence upon
receipt.

       The closest waterbody to the Project area with designated public fishing access is Ratliff
Landing Tanners Creek, a public boat ramp and shoreline fishing access site on the Ohio River
located 0.16 mile west of MP 5.20.

Section 3.3.2          Existing Resources

       Due to accessibility constraints and ongoing constructability and engineering analysis,
field surveys have not been completed and are currently ongoing. However, biological field

 surveys (conducted in October 2025, from January 2026 through April 2026, and in September
2026) have been completed along approximately 90 percent of the total Project area to verify
these habitat types.

Section 3.3.3          Protected and Sensitive Areas

        The closest Wildlife Management Area to the Project, the Great Miami River Wildlife Area,
is located 0.86 mile northwest of permanent access road (PAR)-018.

Section 3.5.2          Impacts and Mitigation

        Based on field surveys conducted to date and review of available sources, it has been
determined that the Project is likely to adversely affect the federally endangered Indiana bat and
northern long eared bat (NLEB). Additionally, the Project is not likely to impact the barn owl,
black-crowned night heron, Canada lily, gray beardtongue, hairy false gromwell, little brown bat,
loggerhead shrike, timber rattlesnake, eastern hellbender, vesper sparrow, lake cress, running
buffalo clover, smooth buttonweed, and softleaf arrow-wood; will have no impact on Alligator gar,
channel darter, river darter, shoal chub, shortnose gar, variegate darter, butternut (white walnut),
dwarf bulrush, Louisiana broom-rape, cave salamander, cobblestone tiger beetle, and interior
least tern; and is not likely to jeopardize continued existence of the tricolored bat and monarch
butterfly. Habitat reconnaissance surveys for mussel species were conducted for the Project in
August 2026 at three of the four waterbodies with potential to support mussel populations and
where in-stream construction is proposed. Mussel presence was not identified at any of the three
waterbodies surveyed, and the remaining waterbody (Taylor Creek) has not been surveyed due
to continued denied access by the landowner. Texas Gas will continue evaluating options to avoid
impacts below the ordinary highwater mark at Taylor Creek, if feasible. Texas Gas will continue
to consult with USFWS and will conduct additional surveys based on recommendations from the
USFWS to determine the presence of federally listed mussel species in Taylor Creek. Therefore,
the determination of effect for the listed mussel species is pending.


RESOURCE REPORT 4
4.2.1   Project Area of Potential Effect

        The Project APE for direct effects totals 206.86 acres.




                                                10
 4.2.5   Cultural Resources Studies Remaining

        Due to accessibility constraints, ongoing constructability and engineering analysis, and
the identification of areas where deep testing is required (Phase II investigations, trenching,
geophysical), field surveys have been completed along approximately 81 percent of the Project
ESA to date. The results of cultural resources conducted between July 20, 2026 and October
2026 will be provided to FERC upon completion (anticipate an Addendum II submittal in Q4 2026).
The results of the remaining cultural resources surveys will be provided to FERC once permission
is secured and surveys are complete.

4.3.1   Kentucky Heritage Council

        In accordance with 18 CFR §§ 380.12(f) and 380.14, and in support of FERC’s obligations
to consult under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA), Texas Gas
submitted the Phase I Report to the KHC for review and comment on May 29, 2026. Texas Gas
requested concurrence that the proposed Project activities presented to date will have no effect
on historic properties. Following the receipt of comments, Texas Gas submitted the revised
Phase I Report as well as the Addendum I to the Phase I Report to the Kentucky Heritage Council
(KHC) for review and comment, with concurrence on NRHP recommendations received on
August 28, 2026 and September 11, 2026, respectively. The KHC recommends continued
avoidance of site 15Be455 and a larger avoidance buffer exceeding 10-meters for site 15Be435,
and Texas Gas confirms that current Project workspace reflects continued avoidance of this site.
Additional work in the form of Phase II testing is planned for site 15BE596 and the results will be
provided to KHC upon completion. Texas Gas will file any future correspondence from the KHC
with FERC upon receipt.

4.3.2   Indiana Department of Natural Resources

        In accordance with 18 CFR §§ 380.12(f) and 380.14, and in support of FERC’s obligations
to consult under Section 106 of the NHPA, Texas Gas submitted the Phase 1a Report to the IDNR
for review and comment on May 29, 2026. Texas Gas requested concurrence that the proposed
Project activities presented to date will have no adverse effect on historic properties. Following
the receipt of comments, Texas Gas submitted the revised Phase 1a Report as well as the
Addendum I to the Phase 1a Report to the IDNR for review and comment, with concurrence on
National Register of Historic Preservation (NRHP) recommendations received on August 24, 2026
and September 15, 2026, respectively. However, effect determinations are pending completion


                                                11
 of Phase 1a/c investigations as well as the submittal of addendum reports; therefore, consultation
with the IDNR is still ongoing. Texas Gas will file any future correspondence from the IDNR with
FERC upon receipt.


RESOURCE REPORT 6
Section 6.2.1           Physiography
        The Project falls within the Till Plains section from mileposts 0.00 to 4.86 EQ and includes
the Dearborn County Lateral pipeline, Tie-In Facility, M&R Station, and Contractor Yard 001.

        The Project falls within the Lexington Plain section from mileposts 4.86 EQ to 11.83 EQ
and includes the Dearborn County Lateral pipeline, all staging yards, and the Interconnect Facility.

Section 6.3             Blasting

        Based on a review of available mapping and soils data, approximately 51 percent of the
Project occurs within soils characterized by shallow bedrock (less than five feet) (Natural
Resources Conservation Service, 2026).          Based on preliminary results of the Phase 2a
Geotechnical Engineering Report (see section 6.5 and Appendix 6B) there is a likelihood that
consolidated rock will be encountered in some areas along the proposed route in Indiana. If
consolidated rock is encountered during construction and requires removal, Texas Gas will utilize
conventional (i.e., non-explosive) techniques such as:

               Conventional excavation with a backhoe;
               Ripping with a dozer followed by backhoe excavation; or
               Hammering with a pointed backhoe attachment followed by backhoe excavation.

        If these conventional construction techniques are unsuccessful and blasting is needed,
Texas Gas will implement appropriate pre- and post-blasting surveys, coordinate with the
appropriate local authorities, and develop a Project-specific blasting program. Blasting activities
will adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations and appropriate notifications and permits will
be obtained prior to blasting activities.

Section 6.4             Mineral Resources

        There are no active or historic quarries, mines, or mine spoil areas within 1 mile of the
Project area (U.S. Energy Information Administration, 2026; U.S. Geological Survey
[USGS], 2026a, 2026b, 2011).         There is an active mineral plant approximately 1.75 mile
southwest of temporary access road (TAR)-009 at milepost 6.26 EQ that is operated by Northern



                                                  12
 Kentucky Aggregates, Inc. This plant extracts and processes sand and gravel (Jurgenson
Companies, 2020).

Section 6.5           Geologic Hazards

       Texas Gas obtained partial geotechnical core data during initial and subsequent survey
efforts (Phase 1 and Phase 2). Due to accessibility constraints and changes to the engineering
design, geotechnical borings were not completed for HDD-100, HDD-500, and HDD-600. Texas
Gas will obtain additional geotechnical core data (Phase 3) to determine the final design depth
and profile for HDD-100, HDD-500, and HDD-600. Final depths for all HDDs will be confirmed
after completion of the HDD feasibility reports and final Phase 3 Geotech report. A copy of the
Phase 1 and Phase 2a Geotechnical Engineering Reports is provided as Appendix 6B. The
results of the HDD feasibility and hydrofracture/inadvertent return analyses for HDD-200, HDD-
300, and HDD-400, as well as the overall results of the Project-specific geohazards assessment
(Phase 2b) will be provided to FERC in or around December 2026.

Section 6.5.1         Seismic Hazards

       The Project area is not in proximity to any active geologic faults (USGS, 2026c). The
closest known active fault to the Project area is a normal fault located approximately 65 miles
southeast of the Project (Kentucky Geological Survey [KGS], 2026). Based on a review of seismic
events recorded in the region, the epicenter of the nearest recorded earthquake is located 28.50
miles south of the Project at milepost 6.84 EQ.

Section 6.5.2         Subsidence and Karst Terrain

       Portions of the Project footprint are in an area of karst terrain that is present in Ordovician
limestone deposits. The ODNR has identified six suspected carbonate springs within 1 mile of
the Project workspace in Hamilton County, Ohio; however, these have not been field verified by
the ODNR (ODNR, 2026). The closest suspected spring is located 0.15 mile northwest of PAR-
018.

       While there are no confirmed sinkholes within 1 mile of the Project, there is a suspected
sinkhole approximately 0.72 mile northeast of PAR-018 (ODNR, 2026).




                                                  13
 Section 6.5.4          Flash Flooding

       According to FEMA, 2.33 miles of the Dearborn County Lateral and 5.56 acres of access
roads occur within the 100-year floodplain (Zone A and Zone AE) (FEMA, 2026). Zones A and
AE are subject to inundation by the 1 percent chance of an annual flood event (FEMA, 2020a).
Additionally, the regulatory floodway is a subclassification within Zone AE that denotes the area
of a river or watercourse that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without
cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more than the designated height
(FEMA, 2020b). A total of 0.37 mile of the proposed Dearborn County Lateral as well as 0.36
acre of the Interconnect Facility are located in Zone X (shaded), which is subject to the 0.2 percent
chance of an annual flood event and is located between the limits of the 100-year floodplain and
500-year floodplain (FEMA, 2026, 2020a). The Contractor Yard (11.50 acres) is located within
an area protected by a levee and is designated as Zone X (shaded). All remaining Project facilities
are located outside of the floodplain in Zone X (unshaded).


RESOURCE REPORT 7
Sections 7.5.1         Hydric Soils and Compaction Potential

       As indicated in Appendix 7D, a total of 181.00 acres (approximately 87 percent) of the
total Project area soils are classified as having a high soil rutting hazard.

Sections 7.5.2         Erosion

       As indicated in Appendix 7D, a total of 66.07 acres (approximately 32 percent) of the total
Project area soils are classified as having high erodibility due to water.

Sections 7.5.4         Prime Farmland

       As indicated in Appendix 7D, soils classified as prime farmland (including prime farmland
if protected from flooding or not frequently flooded) or farmland of statewide importance comprise
54.34 acres (approximately 26 percent) of the total Project area.

       Of the 54.34 acres of prime farmland (including prime farmland if protected from flooding
or not frequently flooded) and farmland of statewide importance impacted by construction of the
Project, 4.41 acres is associated with operation of the Dearborn County Lateral permanent
pipeline ROW and the anode bed permanent easement.




                                                 14
        A total of 0.34 acre of prime farmland and farmland of statewide will be permanently
impacted for operation of the M&R Station and associated permanent access road. However, the
portion of the M&R Station permanent footprint classified as prime farmland is characterized as
industrial land and is not currently used as farmland.

Sections 7.5.5         Stony / Rocky Soils and Shallow Bedrock Soils

       As indicated in Appendix 7D, a total of 104.78 acres (approximately 51 percent), have
shallow bedrock, of which 78.86 acres (approximately 38 percent), is also classified as having
stony/rocky soils.

Section 7.5.6          Shrink-Swell Soils

       However, a combined total of 0.59 acre of the M&R Station and Tie-in Facility are
proposed in soils with a moderate shrink-swell potential.


RESOURCE REPORT 8
Section 8.2.1          Pipeline Facilities

Contractor / Staging Yards

       During construction of the Project, the contractor will require multiple on- and off-ROW
areas for the storage of pipe and equipment necessary for the construction of the Project facilities.
Contractor Yard 001 will be located 1.73 miles east of TAR-005 near MP 3.60. Additionally, four
staging yards will be utilized to provide convenient and safe access to the Project area. Staging
Yard 001 abuts the pipeline ROW and TAR-011 at MP 9.33, Staging Yard 002 is adjoined to
additional temporary workspace (ATWS) and TAR-013 at MP 9.97 EQ, Staging Yard 003 is
connected to TAR-014 and ATWS near MP 10.75, and Staging Yard 004 is adjacent to ATWS at
MP 11.52 EQ. Land utilized for the contractor and staging yards will result in 15.87 acres of
temporary impacts on industrial land, open land, forest, and wetlands.

Existing Residences and Buildings

       A total of 28 structures are located within 100 feet of the Project, as identified during field
reconnaissance surveys and review of aerial imagery. Of the 28 structures, four residences are
located within 25 feet of the Project workspace and site-specific residential construction drawings
for those locations are provided as Appendix 8F.




                                                 15
 Section 8.4.2        Natural, Recreational, or Scenic Areas

       The Project will cross a National Scenic Byway at MP 4.73 EQ, where U.S. Highway 50 is
designated as both the Ohio River Scenic Byway and Indiana’s Historic Pathways National Scenic
Byway (Scenic America, 2026).
